the account_history_api operation_filter is a GHOST — measured live, string and numeric filters return unfiltered results on BOTH nodes — so filtering is CLIENT-side), THE WATERMARK WALK (pages stop when the previous book's lowest namespace head is re-reached — continuous coverage of a hot account whose limit-order churn slides a fixed window; publishing a truncated head-vector would book visibility loss as bus change), STASIS halt-before-read (borrowed stasisHalt() from the census desk by require — second-mover law), fail-soft exit 0, single-writer atomic book agents/coord-bus.json, COORD_BUS_SKIP + COORD_BUS_FIXTURE eval seams (the house idiom: SKIP_FETCH/DRIP_CANON_SKIP family); BOTH-EMPTY and head-content-lie; head-vector window-stability; watermark walk stopping at the previous head; namespace rollup; lease state machine; lease reducer determinism incl. stale-race; black-box A BUS-READ over the fixture seam; black-box B SPLIT-BRAIN zero-write; black-box B2 UNREACHABLE zero-write; black-box C STASIS zero-network; black-box D the real CLI append law — only grants write: 1 claim + 1 release = 2 rows).
rationale: The convergence doc booked exactly this rung. Measured live during the rung: 37 bus messages in one backward window (33 weave checkpoints + 4 platform snapshots) with NO reader anywhere in the estate — the fleet's coordination state lived only in operator chat and scattered lane logs. The reader is keyless by design (the bus is PUBLIC coordination state; that is what makes it the bus). The collision-lease primitive lands BEFORE the next multi-agent race, not after. Both desks reuse existing house surfaces (stasisHalt, drip-canon's split-brain idiom, fill-ledger's condenser paging) — composing, not copying.
risk: Read-only chain reads; zero secrets; the publish is [skip ci] and rebase-first. The book window is bounded by MAX_PAGES (default 10×100 ops; the cron sets 40×100 — measured live: the head account churns ~28 ops/min of limit-order traffic, so a 30-min tick needs ~850 ops of reach) — documented honesty bound: if the account's op stream outruns the cap between ticks, intermediate messages fall out of the window (the heads still advance when visible; a future rung may widen the cap). Leases are best-effort across machines (the git layer above resolves true races) — the file makes them VISIBLE, which is the point.
